chunks: And I bear witness that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) is His slave and His Messenger.
He sent him for the enforcement of His command, for exhausting His plea, and for presenting His warners.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of the Prophet being described as both slave and messenger in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In the Al-Gharra sermon, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) encapsulates the theological essence of prophethood by linking the Prophet’s servitude ('abd) with his messengership (rasul), a duality central to Shia Christology. This passage emphasizes the functional purpose of the Prophet’s mission: to finalize divine authority ('infa' al-amr) and exhaust human excuses ('inha' al-'udhr), thereby establishing the completeness of revelation. The mention of 'delivering warnings' underscores the eschatological dimension of his role, resonating with the Shia emphasis on the Prophet as the ultimate bearer of glad tidings and warnings.

en.sayed-ali-raza: And I stand witness that Muḥammad (blessing of Allāh be on him and his progeny) is His slave and His Prophet.
He sent him for enforcement of His commends, for exhausting His pleas and for presenting warnings (against eternal punishment).
